role: cross-run drift anchor for the CI/CD gate WARN branch; the requirements compare total findings against a previous baseline that no directive produces, so this artifact supplies it
purpose: Persists THIS run's finding totals so the NEXT run's gate can decide its WARN branch. Directive 9 compares total findings against a previous baseline that no directive produces, so without this file WARN is undecidable. Counts only - no finding text, no path, no secret.
run_id_basis: sha256 over four slots concatenated in the fixed order arch-audit, semgrep, taint-analysis, osv-scanner, then truncating the hex digest to its first 16 characters. Each slot is resolved STATUS FIRST: read layer-status.json, and if that layer's status is ERROR the slot carries the deterministic sentinel described in run_id_error_layer_substitution and the artifact is never opened; otherwise the slot carries the artifact's complete bytes including its single terminating LF. Reproduce with: python3 -c "import hashlib,json;st=json.load(open('security-audit/layer-status.json'));P=[('layer_1','findings-layer-1-arch.json'),('layer_2','findings-layer-2-semgrep.json'),('layer_3b','findings-layer-3b-taint.json'),('layer_4','findings-layer-4-osv.json')];print(hashlib.sha256(b''.join((('ERROR:'+k).encode() if st.get(k)=='ERROR' else open('security-audit/'+f,'rb').read()) for k,f in P)).hexdigest()[:16])". Content-addressed and host-independent: identical inputs and identical statuses always yield this identifier, and any edit to any contributing artifact changes it. Hashing hex-encoded intermediates instead of the raw slot bytes yields a different value.

run_id_error_layer_substitution.why: derivation.error_layer_rule states that a layer documented ERROR may legitimately lack its normalized artifact. An identifier recipe that unconditionally opens all four files therefore aborts on exactly the runs the escape hatch exists to permit, and an earlier wording of run_id_basis did precisely that - it described an unconditional read of all four artifacts while the count rule beside it allowed one of them to be absent.
run_id_error_layer_substitution.order_of_operations: Status first. Each layer's status is resolved from layer-status.json BEFORE any attempt to open, stat or probe that layer's artifact. An ERROR-documented artifact is never opened and its absence is never discovered as an error, because it is never looked for.
run_id_error_layer_substitution.sentinel: ERROR:<ledger short-form key>, US-ASCII, with no terminating newline - exactly one of ERROR:layer_1, ERROR:layer_2, ERROR:layer_3b or ERROR:layer_4
run_id_error_layer_substitution.slot_rule: The sentinel occupies that layer's slot in the concatenation. The slot is never omitted and never filled with zero bytes: omitting it would make the ERROR run collide with a three-layer run, and zero bytes would make an ERROR layer indistinguishable from a genuinely empty artifact.
run_id_error_layer_substitution.count_rule: The same layer contributes zero to total_findings, by_layer, by_severity, gate_blocking and advisory, and is named in layers_documented_error, so the identifier and the counts agree on which layers contributed.
run_id_error_layer_substitution.gate_and_publication_effect: A documented-ERROR layer fires the gate's ERROR branch, which outranks BLOCK, WARN and PASS in strict precedence; its records are omitted from the merged report's body rather than substituted with placeholders; and this baseline is withheld rather than published, because publication_lifecycle.withhold_conditions names an ERROR status as its first withholding condition. An ERROR run therefore never becomes the next run's PRIOR comparand.
run_id_error_layer_substitution.missing_without_documented_error: A layer whose artifact is absent while its status is not ERROR is a hard failure. Generation aborts naming that layer, no sentinel is substituted, and no baseline is published. The sentinel is the documented-ERROR escape hatch, never a way to paper over an unexplained absence.
run_id_error_layer_substitution.this_run: layers_documented_error is empty, so all four slots carry artifact bytes. The generalized recipe above was executed and reproduces run_id fe80bf0d9cda5cea exactly, identical to the value the earlier unconditional recipe produced, so this correction changes the algorithm's behaviour only on runs the earlier one could not express.
run_id_error_layer_substitution.sentinel_branch_demonstrated: Simulating layer_2 ERROR against this artifact set yields run_id 35c051de2278e7ed with findings-layer-2-semgrep.json never opened, confirming that the ERROR branch is reachable and that it is distinguishable from the all-present case.

generated_at_meaning: when this run's counts were computed from the four normalized arrays
published_at_meaning: when this snapshot became the published CURRENT baseline, which is necessarily after the merged report existed and after the canonical verification harness passed. The two stamps differ because publication is gated on those two events, not on the moment the counts were available; publication_lifecycle records the ordering and the conditions under which publication is withheld.
codebase_baseline_commit_note: The audited codebase state every layer measured, identical to the value run-metadata.txt and codebase-profile.txt record. Deliberately not the current HEAD, which advances with each artifact commit and is never a measurement basis.
coverage_basis: No record in any contributing layer carries coverage=partial and neither persisted coverage summary reports a partial category, so this run is complete and its totals are a clean anchor. A partial run escalates the verdict to ERROR and its totals must not be adopted as a baseline without noting the partiality.
gate_counts_note: gate_blocking and advisory are recorded as drift provenance only. The gate's BLOCK branch reads findings-layer-3b-taint.json directly; it never reads this file. Under REPRODUCIBILITY the gate-blocking set is the stable anchor across runs, while advisory findings may legitimately vary - which is what the 20 percent tolerance absorbs.

warn_branch.rule: WARN if: no gate-blocking, but total findings exceed previous baseline by >20%.
warn_branch.comparison: next_run.total_findings > previous.total_findings * 1.20 => WARN; otherwise, absent ERROR and gate-blocking findings, PASS
warn_branch.tolerance_provenance: The 20 percent figure is the requirements' own and is the only threshold this artifact carries. The repository declares no security SLA, KPI or coverage threshold, and none is invented here.
warn_branch.precedence: ERROR > BLOCK > WARN > PASS, strict and non-overlapping. A pipeline failure outranks a vulnerability finding, and a gate-blocking finding outranks any count comparison.
warn_branch.sole_consumer: the WARN branch of gate_verdict in findings-merged.json
warn_branch.first_run_semantics: When no PRIOR snapshot exists - as on this run, which creates the artifact - WARN is structurally unreachable and the verdict falls through past it. That is the intended behaviour, not a defect. No synthetic prior baseline is ever fabricated to make WARN reachable: absence is meaningful, and the CURRENT snapshot this run writes is never substituted for the missing PRIOR one.
warn_branch.prior_snapshot_comparand: the PRIOR run's baseline total_findings, never this document's own total_findings

merge_projection.algorithm: Inter-layer-only deduplication on (file, line, cwe) by construction: two findings from the same layer never merge, so each key contributes max(per-layer count) records and corroborated counts the records that absorbed two or more layers. Same-layer collapsing is forbidden because every Layer 4 record shares one lockfile path and line 0, which would fabricate corroborations.
merge_projection.authority: Informational drift diagnostic only. findings-merged.json is authoritative for post-merge figures, and the WARN comparison keys on total_findings, never on these values, so a projection that differs from the merged report cannot change any verdict.
corroboration_examples: Dockerfile:94 CWE-250 - arch-audit and semgrep independently

publication_lifecycle.defect_this_replaces: On this run the CURRENT snapshot was first committed at 612f6d8cd7, author time 2026-08-01T00:00:14Z, which is 36m33s BEFORE the merged report it belongs to at 9c102b6f38, author time 2026-08-01T00:36:47Z, and before any verification had run at all - no canonical harness existed yet. A snapshot published ahead of the merge and the verification it summarises can be adopted as the next run's PRIOR comparand even if that merge or that verification then fails, which silently moves the WARN threshold on the strength of a run that never completed. Ordering was previously described only as read-PRIOR-then-write-CURRENT, which does not constrain publication against the merge or the verification.

phases.name: read PRIOR
phases.action: read the PRIOR snapshot from its trusted source and retain it unmodified for the duration of the run; it is the only comparand of the WARN branch
phases.on_absence: WARN is structurally unreachable, the verdict falls through past it, and no synthetic prior is fabricated

phases.name: hold CURRENT candidate
phases.action: compute this run's counts from the four normalized arrays and hold them as an unpublished candidate; nothing is written to security-audit/baseline.json at this point

phases.name: merge
phases.action: generate findings-merged.json, including its gate verdict, using the PRIOR snapshot retained in phase 1 and never the candidate held in phase 2

phases.name: verify
phases.action: execute security-audit/verify.sh and capture its output; the candidate becomes publishable only if the harness exits 0 with all sixteen checks PASS

phases.name: publish atomically
phases.action: write the candidate to a temporary path in the same directory and rename it over security-audit/baseline.json, so a concurrent reader observes either the PRIOR snapshot or the CURRENT one and never a partially written file

withhold_conditions: any layer status in layer-status.json is ERROR
any contributing layer record or persisted coverage summary reports partial coverage
the verification harness did not exit 0 with all sixteen checks PASS
publication_lifecycle.withhold_effect: The PRIOR snapshot is preserved byte-for-byte and remains the comparand for the following run. A broken, partial or unverified run is never promoted to PRIOR and its counts are never allowed to move the WARN threshold. Withholding is the safe outcome: it leaves the previous threshold in force rather than replacing it with an unvalidated one.

original.conformance: non-conformant with the phase order above

corrected.action: this snapshot is re-published only after the merged report exists and after the canonical harness has run to completion
corrected.counts_unchanged_reason: none of the four normalized arrays was modified by the correction, so every count here is the same measured value; what changed is when this snapshot becomes publishable and the conditions under which it is withheld

preconditions_satisfied_this_run: no layer status is ERROR - layers_documented_error is empty and all six statuses in layer-status.json are OK
coverage is complete - no contributing record carries a partial coverage flag and neither persisted coverage summary reports a partial category
the merge completed - findings-merged.json exists, carries 879 merged records and a gate_verdict of BLOCK
verification passed - security-audit/verify.sh exited 0 with all sixteen checks PASS, captured in security-audit/verify-output.txt

trust_boundary.claim_this_file_supports: The counts recorded here are the actual measured counts of this run's four normalized arrays, and run_id is content-addressed over exactly the slots run_id_basis names.
trust_boundary.claim_this_file_does_not_support: That a PRIOR snapshot presented to a future run is authentic. run_id is self-contained: an author who inflates total_findings can recompute it from the same inputs and the result verifies clean. A self-contained identifier detects accidental drift; it does not detect a deliberate rewrite.
trust_boundary.attack_this_closes: Inflate the PRIOR snapshot's total_findings so that a later run's genuine increase no longer exceeds the 20 percent tolerance, and the WARN branch never fires for that run or any run after it.
prior_snapshot_source_requirements: Load the PRIOR snapshot only from a protected base branch, or from an immutable artifact store keyed to the commit of the job that produced it. Content that the candidate branch can write is never the comparand.
Verify the PRIOR snapshot against an external trusted manifest or signature obtained over a channel the candidate branch cannot write, and bind it to its producing commit.

Treat a PRIOR snapshot that fails that verification, or whose producing commit cannot be established, as ABSENT rather than as trusted. WARN then becomes unreachable, which is safe, instead of comparing against a value an attacker chose.
Never accept a PRIOR snapshot supplied by the branch under review, and never substitute this document's own totals for a missing PRIOR snapshot.
trust_boundary.on_mismatch: A provenance mismatch on the PRIOR snapshot resolves to ERROR, which outranks BLOCK, WARN and PASS in strict precedence, and is never downgraded to a warning or triaged as a finding.
trust_boundary.scope_of_this_work: This audit is read-only and adds no pipeline wiring, so the requirement is stated normatively here rather than implemented. Implementing it means changing CI, which the plan places outside this work.
trust_boundary.residual_risk: Until the PRIOR snapshot arrives over a trusted channel, the WARN branch is trustworthy exactly to the degree that the branch supplying the comparand is trustworthy, and no further.

derivation.excluded_input_reason: The merged report CONSUMES this artifact for its WARN branch. Reading it here would invert the dependency direction and create a cycle, so this artifact is written before the merged report and never reads it.
derivation.total_findings_definition: The sum of the lengths of the four normalized per-layer findings arrays, with any layer documented ERROR in layer-status.json contributing zero.
derivation.equality_with_merged_summary: Verification check 11 defines findings-merged.json _summary counts as that same sum, so total_findings equals _summary.total_findings by construction - no read of the merged report is required to guarantee it.
derivation.error_layer_rule: A layer documented ERROR contributes zero to every count here, is named in layers_documented_error, and may legitimately lack its normalized artifact.
derivation.severity_vocabulary_enforcement: An out-of-vocabulary severity, an unparseable input, a missing input, a non-integer line, a non-boolean gateBlocking or a by_severity total that disagrees with total_findings aborts generation with a specific reason. Nothing is silently coerced and no count is silently zeroed.
derivation.counts_are_actual: Every number here is the actual measured count. Nothing is rounded, padded or trimmed to make a future comparison look favourable.
derivation.severity_inflation_disclosure: The requirements' severity map is applied literally to the SARIF level vocabulary (error->critical, warning->high), which systematically inflates semgrep severities relative to the scanner's own semantics. It shifts by_severity and therefore the count comparison that drives WARN; it never affects BLOCK, which keys exclusively on Layer 3b exploitability. A reviewer comparing baselines should read the skew as intentional and systematic, not as drift.
derivation.inputs_note: Exactly the four normalized per-layer findings arrays. Nothing else contributes a count.
derivation.documented_error_reference: security-audit/layer-status.json - consulted ONLY to learn which layers are documented ERROR, so that such a layer contributes zero. It supplies no count and is not an input to any total here.

provenance.note: These counts are only comparable across runs produced by the same tool versions and the same pinned rule packs. run-metadata.txt carries the full provenance: acquisition sources, rule-pack sizes and stanza counts, per-layer exit codes, durations and every documented version deviation.

constraints.serialization: single-line minified JSON object, compact separators, unescaped Unicode, zero embedded newlines
constraints.path_style: every path named here is repository-relative
constraints.determinism: run_id is content-addressed and therefore identical for identical inputs; generated_at is a wall-clock stamp, so this artifact is intentionally not byte-identical across runs. That is correct: it is a per-run anchor and is not one of the deterministic layers (0, 2, 3a, 4) that the reproducibility mandate binds.

first_run_basis: No baseline artifact exists in any earlier run of this pipeline: this file is created by this run, so there is no PRIOR snapshot to compare against. Derived from the artifact's own history, never from the presence of the file this run itself writes.
consumer_contract: Two distinct temporal roles, never conflated. The PRIOR snapshot is the one left by the preceding run and is the ONLY comparand of the gate's WARN branch. The CURRENT snapshot is this document: it records this run's totals for the NEXT run. Ordering is one-way - read the PRIOR snapshot, decide the verdict, then persist the CURRENT snapshot - so a run can never compare itself against itself, and a broken, partial or ERROR run must never be promoted to PRIOR. On this run the PRIOR snapshot is absent, so WARN is structurally unreachable and the verdict falls through past it.
